newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas prices hold in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas prices hold in sluggish trade.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were little changed Tuesday in light trade, as cold weather continued to support the market in the near-term, market sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices for Wednesday delivery were up one cent to C$1.43-C$1.46 per gigajoule (GJ), as cold weather in western Canada kept buyers relying on the market.
"It's dead out there. Everyone was already expecting this cold weather," one Calgary-based trader said.
Forward month prices were similarly steady to slightly higher. April AECO traded at C$1.45, while summer prices ranged anywhere from C$1.43 to C$1.47 per GJ.

At Sumas, Wash., prices were unchanged at $1.12-$1.17 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), with deals mostly reported done at $1.15. Cooler, overcast weather coupled with a plentiful hydroelectric supply continue to buoy the market, traders said.
At Niagara, prices were also flat at $2.09-$2.14 per mmBtu in sluggish trade.
